paper text.label: dis:sole-two-rails
paper text.text:
Let $\mathcal N$ be a closed regular neighborhood of $H_2$ in the
torus. Its genus is zero or one. In either case, no boundary walk
contains all four attachments~\supp{R12}. The face containing
$H_1'-A$ must therefore have at least two boundary walks. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}, this face is an annulus and
$\mathcal N$ has genus zero.

In each genus-zero rotation, exactly one pair of boundary walks
contains all four attachments between them. One meets $s_1,s_2$
and the other meets $t_1,t_2$, each attachment appearing once~\supp{R12}.
Cap the two boundary circles with disks and draw $s_1s_2$ in one
disk and $t_1t_2$ in the other. This gives a sphere embedding of
$H_1'+E$, contradicting its nonplanarity.

what: Every rotation system of H2, consisting of twins p,q on {s1,s2,s3}, twins r,z on {t1,t2,t3}, and the edge s3t3. Attachments: s1,t1,s2,t2; twins and s3,t3 omitted from attachment sequences. All rotations, including genus two, are recorded; only genera zero and one can occur for a regular neighbourhood inside the torus.
how to read: At each vertex, 'cyclic orders' lists the neighbor orders lexicographically, starting each order with the least neighbor. Rotation systems are numbered from 0 in the order of 'vertices', with the last vertex varying fastest. The entry rows[i] indexes 'distinct rows' for rotation system i. Each row gives the genus (2 - V + E - F)/2 and the sorted attachment sequences of the facial walks. After u->v a walk takes v->w, where w follows u at v. A sequence records every visit to an attachment, starting at the least cyclic shift and keeping the walk direction. For claims up to reversal, take the least cyclic shift of either direction.

claims.statement: H2 has 10 vertices, 13 edges and 64 rotation systems. A rotation with F facial walks has genus (5-F)/2.
In genus one, no boundary walk contains all four attachments s1,t1,s2,t2.
In genus zero, no single boundary walk contains all four attachments. Exactly one pair contains all four between them, with sequences s1,s2 and t1,t2, each attachment appearing once.
In genus zero, the five attachment sequences are {si,tj}, {s1,s2}, {s(3-i)}, {t1,t2}, {t(3-j)} for i,j in {1,2}. Each of the four signatures occurs in four rotations.
